overview.title: Every case counts
overview.context: A case brings together patient details, images and the clinical information used in planning. Orthovet keeps this material in one place, so you can consult your references and continue your analysis with the patient's context at hand.
overview.organization: Name, age, species, breed and weight help identify the patient. Alongside these details, clinical notes record what needs attention and preserve the information that guides your assessment, starting with your first review of the case.
overview.files: Radiographs and supporting documents stay linked to the plan. You can check the files already attached, consult an examination and return to patient details as you review an image, keeping your references together throughout your work.
overview.continuity: When you are ready to continue, the case list gives you a starting point. Use search to find the patient and follow the status of cases in draft, in planning, ready or archived before returning to your analysis.

information.question: What information can I keep in a case?
information.answer: You can bring together patient details, such as name, age, species, breed and weight, alongside clinical notes, radiographs and documents used in planning.

files.question: Do images and documents stay linked to the case?
files.answer: Yes. Radiographs and supporting files stay with the case, so you can consult them alongside patient information while working on the plan.

search.question: How do I find a case to continue planning?
search.answer: Use search in the case list to find the patient. Open the case to consult its details, files and references before continuing your analysis.

progress.question: How do I follow the stage of each case?
progress.answer: The list shows each case's status, so you can follow cases in draft, in planning, ready or archived. This lets you identify the stage before opening a case.
